$comment: Controlled vocabularies. Every tag used anywhere in the corpus must resolve here; tools/validate.mjs enforces it.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.annualReport: March 1 (corporations); LLC annual tax due June 1

CA.name: California
CA.annualReport: Statement of Information within 90 days of formation, then biennially (LLC) or annually (corporation)

TX.name: Texas
TX.annualReport: Public Information Report with the franchise tax report, due May 15

FL.name: Florida
FL.annualReport: Annual report due between January 1 and May 1

NY.name: New York
NY.annualReport: Biennial Statement due every two years in the anniversary month of formation

critical.meaning: Legally required, or its absence creates a defect that is expensive to cure later.

recommended.meaning: Market standard. Omitting it is a deliberate choice, not an oversight.

optional.meaning: Useful in some fact patterns; safe to omit.

insertion.auto: Inserted automatically whenever its conditions are satisfied.
insertion.suggest: Held back from the draft and surfaced by missing-clause detection so the user makes an explicit choice.

agreements.name: Make a simple agreement
agreements.desc: short service agreement and letter of agreement

1.name: 1–4 employees
1.triggers: Workers' compensation, IIPP, wage statements, paid sick leave, minimum wage and overtime

5.name: 5–9 employees
5.triggers: FEHA discrimination and harassment law, CFRA, pregnancy disability leave, harassment prevention training, Fair Chance Act, bereavement and reproductive loss leave, off-duty cannabis protections

10.name: 10–14 employees
10.triggers: Workplace Violence Prevention Plan (the under-10 exemption no longer applies)

15.name: 15–19 employees
15.triggers: Pay scale must appear in job postings; federal Title VII and ADA attach

20.name: 20–49 employees
20.triggers: Federal COBRA replaces Cal-COBRA; San Francisco health care and family-friendly ordinances attach

75.name: 75–99 employees
75.triggers: Cal-WARN mass layoff, relocation, and termination notice

californiaReference.$note: Reference values used by California clause bodies. Dollar figures that change annually are expressed as formulas rather than amounts so the corpus does not go stale between updates.
californiaReference.minimumWageBasis: the state minimum wage in effect on January 1 of the current year, which is adjusted annually
californiaReference.exemptSalaryBasis: twice the state minimum wage for full-time employment, recalculated each January
californiaReference.annualTaxLLC: $800 annual tax, due by the fifteenth day of the fourth month of the taxable year (FTB Form 3522)
californiaReference.annualTaxCorp: $800 minimum franchise tax, with a first-taxable-year exemption for corporations
californiaReference.llcFeeTiers: an additional gross receipts fee once total California income reaches $250,000, stepping up at $500,000, $1,000,000, and $5,000,000 (FTB Form 3536)
californiaReference.sickLeaveAccrual: one hour for every thirty hours worked, with use available from the ninetieth day of employment
californiaReference.sickLeaveMinimum: forty hours or five days per year, whichever is greater, with accrual carrying over subject to a cap of eighty hours or ten days

none.name: No local ordinance / elsewhere in California
none.summary: State law alone applies. Confirm this — California localities adopt ordinances frequently and coverage follows where the employee physically works.

sf.name: San Francisco
sf.summary: The densest local employment regime in the state: health care expenditure, paid parental leave, family friendly workplace, fair chance, salary history, and a local minimum wage, several with their own headcount thresholds and annual reporting.

la.name: Los Angeles
la.summary: Local minimum wage and paid sick leave above the state floor, a fair chance hiring ordinance with its own notice steps, freelance worker protections, and fair work week scheduling rules for larger retail and grocery employers.

sd.name: San Diego
sd.summary: Earned sick leave and minimum wage ordinance above the state floor, with its own accrual, carryover, and notice requirements.

sj.name: San Jose
sj.summary: Local minimum wage plus an opportunity-to-work ordinance requiring existing part-time staff be offered additional hours before new hires are made.

oak.name: Oakland
oak.summary: Local minimum wage, paid sick leave with no annual cap for smaller employers, service charge rules, and a fair chance ordinance.

unsourced.name: Unsourced
unsourced.meaning: Drafted from model knowledge with no citation attached. No independent basis exists for anything it asserts.

single-source.name: Single citation
single-source.meaning: One citation is asserted, and nothing has checked that the cited provision says what the clause says it says.

multi-cited.name: Multiple citations
multi-cited.meaning: More than one citation is asserted. Still self-asserted — several citations written by one author are not corroboration.

search-corroborated.name: Search-corroborated
search-corroborated.meaning: The assertion matched a web search summary drawing on two or more independent sources, with URLs and a check date recorded. No source document was opened and no primary text was read. This is a lead for a reviewer, not a verification.

corroborated.name: Corroborated
corroborated.meaning: Two or more independent secondary sources were opened and read, and each was recorded with a URL and a date. The primary text was still not checked. This sits BELOW the release gate: secondary sources agreeing with each other is not two primary sources.

primary-verified.name: Primary verified
primary-verified.meaning: Checked against the primary text by a named reviewer, with at least TWO primary sources on distinct hosts recorded with URLs and check dates, at least one of them the publisher of the text itself. Two pages on one publisher are one source. A mirror, however faithful, is somebody else's copy and does not count; a law firm reading, however expert, is corroboration and never verification.

releaseGate.$note: Minimum verification level a clause must reach before the engine will draft it into a document. The bar is two primary sources on distinct hosts, at least one of them the publisher of the text, read by a named person and recorded with dates. Everything below that — a single citation, several citations by one author, a search summary, two secondary sources agreeing — is withheld and counted, not silently dropped. Drafting clauses are gated separately on draftingReviewLevels, because the source ladder cannot grade a clause that cites nothing; applying it to all 360 clauses made the 191 drafting clauses permanently unreleasable for a reason that does not apply to them. A clause whose assertsLaw classification is still heuristic clears neither gate.
releaseGate.$draftingNote: Minimum drafting-review level before the engine will draft a non-law-asserting clause. Self-reviewed sits below the gate on purpose. A clause whose assertsLaw classification is still heuristic and unreviewed cannot clear either gate, because nothing yet establishes which ladder it belongs on.

reviewTracks.$note: A clause that states what the law requires and a clause that states a negotiated term fail in different ways and are vetted by different people. Collapsing them is what makes a 360-clause review look impossible; separating them is what makes 'no mistake' reachable.

authority.question: Does the source actually say this, and does it say all of it?
requires: every assertion pinned to an attested source text
authority.failureMode: omission — the headline number is right and the qualifier that decides whether it applies is missing
authority.cannotBeSatisfiedBy: drafting review, reading the clause on its own, or a model re-reading its own output

drafting.question: Is this the term we want, drafted so it does what we intend?
requires: a named drafting reviewer who is not the author
a recorded review date and the scope that was reviewed
the clause makes no claim about what the law requires
the assertsLaw classification itself reviewed, not heuristic
drafting.failureMode: a term that is unfavourable, ambiguous, or unenforceable as written
drafting.cannotBeSatisfiedBy: statutory verification, because the clause asserts no statute

draftingReviewLevels.$comment: A drafting clause asserts no law, so the source ladder cannot grade it — no number of citations makes a negotiated term the right term. This is the ladder it is graded on instead. The two are not interchangeable and neither can borrow the other's evidence: a statute does not tell you whether an indemnity cap is the one you want, and a lawyer's approval does not tell you what a statute says.

unreviewed.name: Unreviewed
unreviewed.meaning: Nobody has read this as a negotiated term. It was drafted from model knowledge, and whether it is the term anyone would want is unknown.

self-reviewed.name: Self-reviewed
self-reviewed.meaning: Read by whoever produced it. Deliberately below the gate: an author checking their own work is not review, for the same reason a second citation by the same author is not corroboration.

practice-corroborated.name: Practice-corroborated
practice-corroborated.meaning: Two things, both mechanical, neither a legal opinion: (1) checked against real, named reference agreements from reputable non-law-firm sources for structural and substantive consistency with market practice, with URLs and fetch dates recorded; (2) run through the corpus's automated internal-consistency checks (terminology agreement between clause bodies and signature blocks, cross-reference validity, mutual-exclusivity of variants). This is evidence that the term is not obviously wrong or internally inconsistent. It is NOT legal review, is deliberately still below the release gate, and cannot be produced by an author self-certifying — see corroboration.mjs for what is actually required.

counsel-reviewed.name: Counsel-reviewed
counsel-reviewed.meaning: Read by a named lawyer other than the author, on a recorded date, against a stated scope. The finding is that the clause does what it says and is enforceable as written — not that it is the deal you want. Nothing below this rank, however much corroboration it carries, may be described to a user as reviewed by a lawyer.

counsel-approved.name: Counsel-approved
counsel-approved.meaning: A named lawyer approves this as the term to use for the stated package and posture. A commercial judgement on top of the review, not a substitute for it.

sourceTiers.$comment: Who publishes a source decides what it can prove. Authoritative classification lives in tools/sources.mjs; this is the summary. The test for a primary source: if this host and every other host disagreed, whose version would be the law?

publisher.meaning: the sovereign's own text — the legislature, the code office, the register, the court

agency.meaning: the agency administering the rule, on its own site. Primary for its forms, procedures and deadlines; not for what a statute means

mirror.meaning: a faithful republisher. Usually right, still a copy, with its own transcription errors and its own update schedule

secondary.meaning: an expert reading — a law firm, an accounting firm, a trade body. Corroboration; never verification
